lectures.title: Binary Tree Traversal - Level Order Traversal

cues.en: Now in this lecture we are going to look at binary tree traversal.
Now there are various ways of traversal in case of trees.
But here in this lecture we are going to talk about specific type which will be used in the next lecture
inside the insert method.
That's why I decided to first explain the binary tree traversal.
Then we will continue to the insert method.
Then after that we will look at different types of the binary tree traversal.
Now when we say tree traversal, it means that we have to visit all nodes of the binary tree.
Now you might be interested that why we have various types of tree traversal.
Now this is because when we are traversing the tree, we have to visit all nodes of the tree.
So in which order we are going to visit the all nodes.
So we will start from here.
Then go to the for example n two.
Then from here we will go to n three, then n four or we will start from here.
Then go to n two, then go to n4.
Then go to n three.
Or we can do it like this.
From n one we can go to n three, then n seven N7 and continue like this.
So the order of the visit will define the type of the traversal.
Now there are two main types of the tree traversal.
First is the depth first search and the second one is breadth first search.
Now in depth first search, we have preorder traversal, in-order traversal, postorder traversal,
and in breadth first search we have level order traversal and level order traversal will be used in
insert method.
That's why first I will start with the level order traversal.
Now what is level order traversal?
As the name implies, it visits the nodes level by level.
So if we look at this binary tree over here, we see that this is going to be the level one.
Then we have level two.
Then we have level three.
So for this binary tree we have three levels.
In the first level we have root.
Then in the second level we have the children of the root.
Then in the third level we have the grandchildren of the root.
And it continues like this.
Now in case of tree traversal, we will start from the first level and visit the root node.
Then we will continue to the second level and start from the left child and continue to the right child
and visit all children over here.
Then we will continue to the third level.
In this case also, we will start from the left child of the left parent.
So this is going to be the left child then visiting all nodes from left to right.
So this is going to be the order of the visit that we have in case of the level order traversal.
So if we look at with the arrow the order will be like this.
We are starting from n1 then n two and three and four and five and six and seven.
So this is going to be the order of the traversal in case of level order traversal.
So let's look at how we are going to implement this.
So in case of level order traversal we are going to use another data structure which is going to be
the queue to help us because queue works first in first out manner.
That's the logic that we need over here.
So first I'm going to create a queue data structure.
Then inside this queue data structure I will enqueue the first node which is going to be the N1.
Then we are going to take this node out and we will print out this one to the console mentioning that
we have visited this node, then we are going to go ahead and check that if N1 has children, we are
going to go ahead and enqueue the children of N1 this queue over here.
So we are going to start from the left.
So we see that for N1 we have left and right children.
So first we are going to enqueue the left child.
Then we are going to incur the right child.
So we know that in case of the queue the first one that comes will be in the first in the queue.
So that is the node will be come out first.
Then in the next step we are going to go ahead and dequeue the element from the queue.
So this is going to be the N2 because this is the first node over here in this queue.
Then we are going to print out and use value to the console which means that we have visited this node.
Then we will check that if n2 has children or not.
So we see that it has left and right child.
So that's why we are going to take N4 and N5, which are the children of N2, and queue them from left
to right to the this queue over here.
So this is going to enqueue N4 and N5 to this queue, then we will continue to dequeue the nodes from
this queue.
Now if we dequeue the node it's going to be N3.
So we are going to print out n3 value to the console saying that we have visited this.
Then we are going to check that if N3 has children or not, we see that it has N6 and N7.
So we are going to take left and right child and enqueue them to the queue over here, which is going
to be from left to right.
So that's why the element will be inserted like this.
First we will have left child which is N6.
Then we will have N7.
Then one more time we are going to continue to dequeue the elements from the queue, which is going
to be N4.
So we are going to print out in force value to the console.
Then we will check that if N4 has children or not, we see that it is not.
That's why we will continue to dequeue the elements from the queue.
So the next element is going to be n five, and we are going to print out N5 value to the console.
Then we are going to check that if N5 has children or not we see that it doesn't have.
That's why we will dequeue another element which is going to be N6.
And hit again.
The first thing that we are going to do, we are going to print out N6 value to the console.
Then we are going to check that if N6 has children or not, we see that it is not.
That's why we are going to continue to take the next element from the queue.
In this case it is N7.
So we are going to print out N7 to the console.
Then we will check that if N7 has children or not, we see that it is not.
That's why we will continue to the next step.
So in the next step we see that the queue is empty.
So we don't have any element for dequeuing.
That's why our operation will stop over here.
So in this case you see that we have visited the elements in the level order.
So in the first level we have n1.
So the first element that we have visited is n1.
Then in the second level we have n2 and n3.
So the next elements that we have visited n2 and n3.
Then we have in four and five and six and in seven.
And that's the order that we have visited all elements.
So that is the logic of the level order traversal.
Now in the next lecture we are going to take this logic and implement this in practice.
